title: The summer sun burns under its appointed dominion
summary_md: Enoch turns from winter to the heat of summer, and again the point is creation under command: *And again, observe ye the days of summer how the sun is above the earth over against it. And you seek shade and shelter by reason of the heat of the sun, and the earth also burns with growing heat, and so you cannot tread on the earth, or on a rock by reason of its heat.* (1 Enoch 4:1). The Psalmist sees the same sun keeping its appointed round: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). The wisdom of the apocrypha describes that very midday scorching: *At noon it parcheth the country, and who can abide the burning heat thereof?* (Ecclesiasticus 43:3), and confesses who set it running: *Great is Yahuah (God) that made it; and at his commandment runs hastily.* (Ecclesiasticus 43:5). Jubilees grounds the sun's dominion in the fourth-day decree, where it is appointed to rule and to mark the feasts: *And Elohim (God) appointed the sun to be a great sign on the earth for days and for sabbaths and for months and for feasts and for years and for sabbaths of years and for jubilees and for all seasons of the years.* (Jubilees 2:9). The heat of the sun is not a terror loose in the world. It keeps the law the Creator gave it, the same law the Watchers are about to abandon.
note: Quote now sits at 4:1 (the old 3:2 is gone); prose lightly mended.

title: Much blood shed, and the voice of crying reaches heaven
summary_md: The four watching archangels look down and see the ruin of Genesis 6 as it happens: *And then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw much blood being shed upon the earth, and all lawlessness being wrought upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 9:1). What they say to one another is that the earth itself has become a cry: *And they said one to another: ‘The earth made without inhabitant cries the voice of their cryings up to the gates of heaven.* (1 Enoch 9:2). The souls of the slain are still crying when the angels bring the case before the throne: *And now, behold, the souls of those who have died are crying and making their suit to the gates of heaven, and their lamentations have ascended: and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds which are wrought on the earth.* (1 Enoch 9:10). The canon gives the same indictment of the same age: *And GOD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually* (Genesis 6:5); *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence* (Genesis 6:11). Blood crying up from the ground is older than the flood, for Yahuah (God) heard it first from a field: *the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground* (Genesis 4:10). Jubilees names the same cause for the same judgement: *every one sold himself to work iniquity and to shed much blood, and the earth was filled with iniquity* (Jubilees 7:23). The angels' grief over shed blood is the Creator's own grief, the grief that *grieved him at his heart* (Genesis 6:6). His order had been broken, and the cry that reached heaven was the earth asking him to set it right.
note: Old 9:2 was invented; re-formed on the live 9:2 and 9:10.

title: The abyss of fire and the destruction of the reprobate spirits
summary_md: The Watchers, and everyone condemned with them, are led away to a prison of fire that has no end: *In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever. And whosoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations. And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.* (1 Enoch 10:13-15). Revelation shows the same sealed prison and the same fire at the end of it: *And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years* (Revelation 20:1–2); *And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more* (Revelation 20:3). The spirits of the reprobate are the evil spirits that went out from the slain giants, the same unclean powers the canon knows, and Jubilees asks that they be locked away from the righteous: *imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant* (Jubilees 10:5). The command given to Gabriel earlier in the chapter is the twin of this one: *Proceed against the bastards and the reprobates, and against the children of fornication: and destroy [the children of fornication and] the children of the Watchers from amongst men [and cause them to go forth]: send them one against the other that they may destroy each other in battle: for length of days shall they not have.* (1 Enoch 10:9). This is judgement on rebellion, and it falls on the ones who corrupted the earth, never on those who kept the covenant.
note: Old 11:3 is gone; quoted the live run 10:13-15 as one citation and 10:9 in full.

title: The plant of righteousness — the earth tilled and full of blessing
summary_md: After judgement comes restoration: *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16); *And then shall all the righteous escape, And shall live till they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace.* (1 Enoch 10:17); *And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.* (1 Enoch 10:18); *And all desirable trees shall be planted on it, and they shall plant vines on it: and the vine which they plant thereon shall yield wine in abundance, and as for all the seed which is sown thereon each measure (of it) shall bear a thousand, and each measure of olives shall yield ten presses of oil.* (1 Enoch 10:19). This is the fruitfulness of the kingdom the prophets foresaw, and the ones who enjoy it are a people, a planting Yahuah (God) chose, which is why the plant is called righteousness and truth rather than a crowd that chose itself. Isaiah promises the same long-lived, vineyard-keeping seed: *And they shall build houses, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them* (Isaiah 65:21); *for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands* (Isaiah 65:22); *for they are the seed of the blessed of Yahuah (LORD), and their offspring with them* (Isaiah 65:23). Amos sees the wine overflowing the very mountains: *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him that soweth seed; and the mountains shall drop sweet wine, and all the hills shall melt* (Amos 9:13). Jubilees names the renewal at the root: *And He made for all His works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever, but should be all righteous each in his kind alway* (Jubilees 5:11). The plant of righteousness is the regathered, covenant-keeping people whom Yahuah replants in the cleansed land.
note: Quotes moved from the vanished 11:6-9 to the live 10:16-19 in full; one sentence smoothed.

title: The earth cleansed — all nations worship the One Yahuah
summary_md: The chapter closes with the whole creation purged and turned to worship: *And cleanse thou the earth from all oppression, and from all unrighteousness, and from all sin, and from all godlessness: and all the uncleanness that is wrought upon the earth destroy from off the earth.* (1 Enoch 10:20); *And all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.* (1 Enoch 10:21); *And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment, and from all torment, and I will never again send (them) upon it from generation to generation and for ever.* (1 Enoch 10:22). This is where the prophets end the matter too, with Yahuah (God) alone as king and every nation turned to him. Zephaniah hears one tongue: *For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD), to serve him with one consent* (Zephaniah 3:9). Zechariah seals the One Name: *And Yahuah (LORD) shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Yahuah (LORD), and his name one* (Zechariah 14:9). The Psalm sings the nations bowing: *All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto Yahuah (LORD): and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee* (Psalm 22:27). And Isaiah shows them flowing up to learn His ways — *and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Yahuah (LORD) from Jerusalem* (Isaiah 2:3): the nations worship by coming under the Torah that goes forth from Zion, not by abolishing it. The cleansing of the earth and the worship of all nations are one act of the same Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and the one does not come without the other.
note: Quotes moved from the vanished 11:10-12 to the live 10:20-22 in full; prose smoothed.

title: The Watchers' petition refused — reserved in chains unto judgement
summary_md: The trembling Watchers ask Enoch to draft their appeal: *And they besought me to draw up a petition for them that they might find forgiveness, and to read their petition in the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of heaven.* (1 Enoch 13:4). Yet Azazel has already been told plainly how it will go: *And thou shalt not have toleration nor request granted to thee, because of the unrighteousness which thou hast taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin which thou hast shown to men.’* (1 Enoch 13:2). The refusal was decreed in the previous chapter before any petition was written: *And no request that they (i.e. their fathers) make of thee shall be granted unto their fathers on their behalf; for they hope to live an eternal life, and that each one of them will live five hundred years.’* (1 Enoch 10:10). The canon holds the same doctrine of the bound Watchers. Isaiah sees that host shut away and kept for an appointed day: *And it shall come to pass in that day, that Yahuah (LORD) shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high... And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited* (Isaiah 24:21-22). The apostles carry it forward without softening a word of it: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6), and *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). There is no appeal for these and no release before the day. They are held for judgement, not pardoned, and when Jude and Peter write it down they are reading what Enoch wrote.
note: Old 13:4 was the corrupt wording; re-quoted from the live 13:4, 13:2 and 10:10 in full; close smoothed.

title: Enoch the scribe — the petition written, the reprimand returned, and iniquity carried away
summary_md: Enoch becomes the scribe who carries the Watchers' plea to the throne: *Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer in regard to their spirits and their deeds individually and in regard to their requests that they should have forgiveness and length.* (1 Enoch 13:6). He reads it until he sleeps, and the answer comes back as a vision: *And behold a dream came to me, and visions fell down upon me, and I saw visions of chastisement, and a voice came bidding (me) I to tell it to the sons of heaven, and reprimand them.* (1 Enoch 13:8). So the scribe who wrote the appeal comes back with the verdict instead: *And I recounted before them all the visions which I had seen in sleep, and I began to speak the words of righteousness, and to reprimand the heavenly Watchers.* (1 Enoch 13:10). The book that follows carries that commission in its very title: *The book of the words of righteousness, and of the reprimand of the eternal Watchers in accordance with the command of the Holy Great One in that vision.* (1 Enoch 14:1). The appeal could never stand. Jubilees says the fathers were kept alive only long enough to watch their sons fall, and were then bound: *And their fathers were witnesses (of their destruction), and after this they were bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation when judgment is executed on all those who have corrupted their ways* (Jubilees 5:10). The Torah had already shown how guilt leaves the camp. It is not pardoned where it stands; it is laid on a head and carried away into the wilderness: *And the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a land not inhabited: and he shall let go the goat in the wilderness* (Leviticus 16:22). That goat for Azazel is the same Azazel chapter 10 binds in the desert, and the sin he taught is removed by judgement, not by a petition for patience. The way of atonement belongs to the Creator, and it was never the rebel's to negotiate.
note: Old 13:10 and 14:1 were corrupt wording; re-formed on the live 13:6, 13:8, 13:10, 14:1.

title: The throne in the house of heaven — crystal, wheels like the sun, and streams of flaming fire
summary_md: Enoch is carried up into the house of the Creator and sees it built of fire: *And I went into the tongues of fire and drew nigh to a large house which was built of crystals: and the walls of the house were like a tesselated floor (made) of crystals, and its groundwork was of crystal.* (1 Enoch 14:10). Inside it a second house opens, and then the throne itself: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim.* (1 Enoch 14:18), *And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon.* (1 Enoch 14:19), *And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:20). The prophets saw this same throne. Ezekiel beheld *the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it.* (Ezekiel 1:26), with the fire round about it: *And I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it, from the appearance of his loins even upward, and from the appearance of his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and it had brightness round about.* (Ezekiel 1:27). Daniel saw the Ancient of days sit down on it, with the same wheels and the same white raiment: *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.* (Daniel 7:9), *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). John's Revelation closes the circle: *a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne... and out of the throne proceeded lightnings and thunderings and voices* (Revelation 4:2,5). It ain't new. The crystal, the wheels like the sun, the stream of fire, the raiment whiter than snow and the ten thousand times ten thousand are one throne seen by Enoch, Ezekiel, Daniel and John, and the order it rules has not changed hands.
note: Old 14:8 and 14:15 quotes were corrupt (the second was really 18:8); re-formed on the live 14:10, 14:18-20 with Ezekiel 1:27 and Daniel 7:9-10 in full from the index.

title: Streams of fire from the throne — the Great Glory whom no angel and no flesh can behold
summary_md: At the end of the throne vision Enoch tells what no creature can bear to look at: *And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon.* (1 Enoch 14:19), *And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:20), *None of the angels could enter and could behold His face by reason of the magnificence and glory and no flesh could behold Him.* (1 Enoch 14:21). Even the host that never leaves him stands at a distance: *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). This is the same word Moses was given on the mountain: *And he said, You can not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.* (Exodus 33:20). Isaiah saw the seraphim covering their faces before that throne: *Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.* (Isaiah 6:2). Daniel saw the same fiery stream and the same uncounted host: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). And John tells us how any man has ever seen him at all: *No man has seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him.* (John 1:18). The Great Glory whom no angel and no flesh can look upon is the Father, and the one who calls Enoch by name out of that fire, *Come hither, Enoch, and hear my word* (1 Enoch 14:24), is how the unseen one has always made himself heard.
note: Anchor 14:19-21 is the throne in the live text, not the star-prison (that thought lives at 18:13-16 and 21:3-10, carried by the chapter-18 and -21 threads). Re-formed on the live anchor; new title. Canon added from the index: Exodus 33:20, Isaiah 6:2, Daniel 7:10, John 1:18.

title: Enoch's commission: the Watchers should not be interceded for
summary_md: Enoch, sent up by the trembling Watchers to plead their case, is met at the throne with the verdict already settled, and with a commission that turns the whole errand around: *And He answered and said to me, and I heard His voice: ‘Fear not, Enoch, thou righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach hither and hear my voice.* (1 Enoch 15:1), *And go, say to the Watchers of heaven, who have sent thee to intercede for them: "You should intercede for men, and not men for you:* (1 Enoch 15:2). The ones who were made to stand before the throne on behalf of men had sent a man to stand there for them, and the Creator will not have the order of his house inverted. The petition is refused because these are not frail men asking mercy but heavenly beings who left their station, and the apostles keep the sentence exactly as Enoch heard it: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6), and again *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). Jubilees records the prayer Yahuah (God) does answer in that same matter, and it is not the Watchers' prayer but Noah's: *and as for these spirits which are living, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant* (Jubilees 10:5). Jude and Peter did not invent the doctrine of the bound angels. They were reading Enoch, and the man who carried the refusal back down to the Watchers was the scribe of righteousness, the one who walked with Elohim (God) while they walked away from him.
note: Degraded closing prose removed; 15:1-2 quoted in full, the thought kept.

title: The union the Watchers should never have made
summary_md: Enoch's commission names the crime to the Watchers' faces: *Wherefore have ye left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons?* (1 Enoch 15:3), *And though ye were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those also do who die and perish.* (1 Enoch 15:4). And the reason it was never permitted them is given in the same breath: *And therefore I have not appointed wives for you; for as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling.* (1 Enoch 15:7). None of this is a myth grafted onto Scripture. It is Genesis 6 told with the names filled in. Moses wrote it plainly: *That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose* (Genesis 6:2), and *There were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:4). The sin is that beings who had a dwelling appointed in heaven left it to take what was appointed for flesh, and that is exactly how Jude reads it: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). Jubilees keeps the same testimony, that *the Watchers against the law of their ordinances went a whoring after the daughters of men, and took themselves wives of all which they chose: and they made the beginning of uncleanness* (Jubilees 7:21). Genesis, Enoch, Jude and Jubilees are describing one descent and one defilement, and the boundary that was crossed was the Creator's own ordinance for where each kind of creature should dwell.
note: Old 16:2 quote was corrupt wording of 15:3-4; re-formed on the live 15:3, 15:4, 15:7.

title: The mysteries that work destruction
summary_md: The Watchers did not only defile themselves; they handed down forbidden knowledge: *“You have been in heaven, but all the mysteries had not yet been revealed to you, and you knew worthless ones, and these in the hardness of your hearts you have made known to the women, and through these mysteries women and men work much evil on earth."* (1 Enoch 16:3). This is the seed-war sown — corrupting arts taught against the Creator's order, multiplying ruin. The Wisdom of Solomon traces the same chain, that *the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life* (the Wisdom of Solomon 14:12), and that those who *used secret ceremonies, or made revellings of strange rites* thereby *kept neither lives nor marriages any longer undefiled* (the Wisdom of Solomon 14:23-24). Peter sets the same pattern in the last days: false teachers *who privily shall bring in damnable heresies* (2 Peter 2:1), so that *by reason of whom the way of truth shall be evil spoken of* (2 Peter 2:2). Worthless mysteries made known to the unguarded are how this evil has always spread, and the Torah still stands as the boundary the Watchers crossed when they taught them.
note: Live 16:3 already in place; closing sentence mended to the new words (evil, made known).

title: Evil spirits from the giants, seeking rest
summary_md: Chapter 16 follows directly from the judgement just declared, that the slain giants leave behind spirits with no flesh to live in: *And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences.* (1 Enoch 15:11), and that they *shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated* (1 Enoch 16:1). Yahusha names exactly these wandering spirits: *When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none* (Matthew 12:43). The dry-place wanderer with no body to dwell in is the giant-spirit of Enoch's account — and the warning that *the last state of that man is worse than the first* (Matthew 12:45) shows the same campaign of destruction Enoch describes still running. Peter confirms the binding that holds the fallen Watchers behind these spirits: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). The Watchers are chained while the spirits of their offspring are loosed for a time, and the Gospels did not invent the origin of the evil spirits; they carried it forward from Enoch.
note: The old phrase sat at 15:11 but the words are 16:1; quoted 15:11 and 16:1 from the live text; close smoothed.

title: The great darkness and the waters of the deep
summary_md: Enoch is led past the edge of the world men know: *I saw the great rivers and came to the great river and to the great darkness, and went to the place where no flesh walks.* (1 Enoch 17:6). He sees where the waters are kept: *I saw the mountains of the darkness of winter and the place whence all the waters of the deep flow.* (1 Enoch 17:7), *I saw the mouths of all the rivers of the earth and the mouth of the deep.* (1 Enoch 17:8). And the next thing he says about it is that none of it is loose. It was furnished and founded: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth.* (1 Enoch 18:1). This is the very tour Yahuah (God) gives Job out of the whirlwind. The place where no flesh walks is the door Job was asked about and had never entered: *Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?* (Job 38:16). The treasuries Enoch keeps being shown are Job's hidden stores: *Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,* (Job 38:22). And the wisdom that furnished the world and set it on its foundations is the psalmist's, the one who *stretchest out the heavens like a curtain: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters* (Psalm 104:2-3). The Creator's order reaches all the way down to the mouth of the deep. The Watchers broke that order where they stood, and they could not unmake one river of it.
note: Old 17:8 "ordered all creation by His wisdom" was invented; the live thought is 18:1. Re-formed on 17:6-8 + 18:1; stray "quoted of v2" apparatus removed.

title: The cornerstone of the earth and the pillars of heaven
summary_md: The journey shows Enoch how the world is held together: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2), and *And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:3). It ain't new. Job is asked the same questions from the whirlwind: *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* (Job 38:4), and *Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;* (Job 38:6) — Enoch is shown the very cornerstone Job could not name. The pillars are Job's too: *The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.* (Job 26:11). And the unmoveable foundation is the psalm's: *Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.* (Psalms 104:5). The Creator's own architecture holds the world in place, and it is the same wise order the rebel host could not overthrow.
note: Quotes already on the live 18:2-3 (the old 17:9-10 are gone); prose smoothed.

title: The throne-mountain of sapphire
summary_md: Among the seven mountains of precious stones Enoch sees one that towers above the rest: *But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Elohim (God), of alabaster, and the summit of the throne was of sapphire.* (1 Enoch 18:8). The sapphire throne is the canon's own picture of the place where Yahuah (God) sits. When the elders of Yashar'el went up the mountain they saw it underfoot: *And they saw the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel): and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone, and as it were the body of heaven in his clearness.* (Exodus 24:10). And Ezekiel, lifted to the firmament, saw the throne itself: *And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone* (Ezekiel 1:26). Enoch's middle mountain is no pagan peak. It is shaped like the sapphire throne the Tanakh already knows, the seat of the Creator whose order the whole journey keeps displaying.
note: Quote already on the live 18:8 (old 17:15 gone); prose smoothed, parenthetical added.

title: The prison of the stars bound till judgement
summary_md: Beyond the waste place Enoch sees the prison-house of the rebel host: *I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:13-14), *And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:15), *And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’* (1 Enoch 18:16). He is shown the same place again a few chapters on, and Uriel gives him the same answer: *These are of the number of the stars of heaven, which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord), and are bound here till ten thousand years, the time entailed by their sins, are consummated.’* (1 Enoch 21:6). Their crime is breaking the fixed order of the Creator, the decree the psalm says the stars cannot transgress: *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalms 148:6). The apostles carry the binding forward as settled doctrine. These are the *wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever.* (Jude 1:13), the *angels that sinned... cast... down to hell, and delivered... into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment:* (2 Peter 2:4). Isaiah names the same prison and the same delayed reckoning: *Yahuah (LORD) shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high... they shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited.* (Isaiah 24:21). The host is not destroyed yet. It is held, bound until the reckoning, the same way Revelation binds the dragon (Revelation 20:2). The order they transgressed still stands, and the judgement on the transgression is still coming.
note: Quotes on the live 18:13-16; the duplicated 18:16 (old 21:7) replaced with the live 21:6; stray apparatus removed.

title: The treasuries of the winds — the world founded by wisdom
summary_md: Enoch is shown the storehouses from which the Creator furnishes the world: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth.* (1 Enoch 18:1). The canon keeps the same chambered winds and the same founding by wisdom. Jeremiah names the very storehouses Enoch saw: *He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and hath stretched out the heavens by his discretion.* (Jeremiah 10:12), *and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasures.* (Jeremiah 10:13). Wisdom herself stands at the founding, *When he established the clouds above: when he strengthened the fountains of the deep:* (Proverbs 8:28), and the winds carry the Creator in the psalm, *who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind:* (Psalm 104:3). What Enoch is looking at is order, not blind nature, and that matters for what comes later in the same chapter. The rebellion of the stars that did not come forth at their appointed times is a rebellion against this founding, against the hand that furnished the winds and set the earth on its foundations. The treasuries Enoch toured are the ones the prophets and the psalmist had already confessed.
note: Old 18:1 was corrupt wording; re-quoted the live 18:1 and smoothed the close.

title: The cornerstone of the earth and the pillars of heaven
summary_md: Enoch is shown the load-bearing structure of the world: *And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:2), *And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:3). This is the Creator's catechism to Job, point for point. He demands, *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.* (Job 38:4), and asks who laid *the corner stone thereof;* (Job 38:6) — the very cornerstone Enoch is shown — *When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim (God) shouted for joy?* (Job 38:7). Wisdom set the same bound: *When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:* (Proverbs 8:29), and the psalmist confesses Him *Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.* (Psalm 104:5). The world has a fixed and founded order, and the rebellion the chapter turns to next is a crime against that architecture, not a flaw in it.
note: Live 18:2 already in place (corner-stone); close smoothed.

title: A prison for the stars and the host of heaven, held to the reckoning
summary_md: At the end of heaven and earth Enoch is shown the holding-place of the rebel host: *And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.* (1 Enoch 18:12), *I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:13-14). They are not destroyed there. They are kept: *And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’* (1 Enoch 18:16). Isaiah sees the same host shut in the same pit and held over for a later visitation: *And it shall come to pass in that day, that Yahuah (LORD) shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth.* (Isaiah 24:21), *And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited.* (Isaiah 24:22). Peter and Jude carry the same chains forward: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;* (2 Peter 2:4), *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* (Jude 1:6). The rebel host is bound and held for the reckoning, the way Sheol holds the dead until they are visited, and the day that visits the one will visit the other.
note: Degraded "framework holds" close removed; live 18:12-14, 18:16 quoted in full.

title: The prison of the angels — held till the great day
summary_md: Beyond the mountains Enoch sees the abyss itself: *And I saw a deep abyss, with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.* (1 Enoch 18:11). He comes to it again on the later journey, and it is worse the second time: *And from thence I went to another place, which was still more horrible than the former, and I saw a horrible thing: a great fire there which burnt and blazed, and the place was cleft as far as the abyss, being full of great descending columns of fire: neither its extent or magnitude could I see, nor could I conjecture.* (1 Enoch 21:7). When he asks, Uriel tells him what it is for: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Revelation shows the same pattern of binding and holding at the great reckoning. The rebel is *cast into the bottomless pit, and shut up, and set a seal upon him* (Revelation 20:3), and at the last *the books were opened* and *the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). The abyss is a prison, not the final sentence. The bound host is kept there until the judgement of the great day, the same reckoning that calls the dead back out of Sheol to be judged.
note: Old 18:15/18:18/21:11 citations were corrupt; re-formed on the live 18:11, 21:7, 21:10 (quoted once); degraded close removed.

title: The women became sirens — destruction through the mysteries
summary_md: Uriel's vision closes the matter of the wives: *And the women also of the angels who went astray shall become sirens.’* (1 Enoch 19:2). The judgement falls not only on the Watchers but on the corruption that ran through the women they took, for Enoch had already been told what the Watchers handed them: *“You have been in heaven, but all the mysteries had not yet been revealed to you, and you knew worthless ones, and these in the hardness of your hearts you have made known to the women, and through these mysteries women and men work much evil on earth."* (1 Enoch 16:3). The pattern is woven through the Tanakh: when Yashar'el *joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.* (Psalms 106:28), the seduction into demon-sacrifice ran by exactly this snare. Sha'ul names the spirits behind it for the assembly: *Ye cannot drink the cup of Yahuah (Lord), and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of Yahuah's (Lord's) table, and of the table of devils.* (1 Corinthians 10:21). The siren is the lie made beautiful, and her singers stand under the same sentence as the ones who taught them: *And Uriel said to me: ‘Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.* (1 Enoch 19:1).
note: Live 16:3 and 19:1 already in place; the two joining sentences mended to the new words.

title: Michael, set over the best part of mankind
summary_md: Of the seven, Enoch singles out one: *Michael, one of the holy angels, to wit, he that is set over the best part of mankind and over chaos.* (1 Enoch 20:5) Daniel knows him by name and office — the prince who contends for Yahuah's covenant people: *but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me* (Daniel 10:13), *there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael your prince* (Daniel 10:21), and at the end *at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people* (Daniel 12:1) — set over the elect, the very 'best part of mankind' Enoch names. Revelation shows that same prince at war against the rebel host: *And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels* (Revelation 12:7). And Enoch himself names Michael again, first among the four presences at the throne: *And he said to me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long- suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’* (1 Enoch 40:9). None of this moves the covenant to another people. Michael stands for the children of Daniel's people, the covenant nation that is gathered and kept, and the prince of the loyal host guards that seed against the dragon's war on it until the reckoning.
note: Live 20:5 already in place ("honoured" dropped from the quote); close rewritten without the dropped word and without the shouting capitals.

title: The hollow places where the dead are gathered till judgement
summary_md: In the great mountain of the West Enoch finds the waiting-place of all the dead: *Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said unto me: ‘These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here.* (1 Enoch 22:3), and they are held *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). The dead are not dissolved into nothing, and they have not yet come to the final verdict. They are gathered, aware, and waiting, and Yahusha (Jesus) tells the same story. The beggar dies and *was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried* (Luke 16:22) — two estates in one holding-place — and between them runs Enoch's very division: *between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence* (Luke 16:26). Sheol holds the dead apart, each according to his way, until the appointed reckoning. The grave is custody, and it is not the final word.
note: Live 22:3-4 already in place; prose smoothed.

title: Abel's spirit still making suit till judgement
summary_md: Among the gathered dead one spirit will not be silent: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit.* (1 Enoch 22:5). Enoch asks whose voice it is, and Raphael names him: *And he answered me saying: ‘This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.’* (1 Enoch 22:7). A whole hollow is set apart for the ones who died that way: *And such a division has been made for the spirits of those who make their suit, who make disclosures concerning their destruction, when they were slain in the days of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 22:12). This is Genesis pressed open. From the ground itself Yahuah (LORD) had already said, *the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground* (Genesis 4:10), and that cry did not stop when Abel died. It went up as a suit for justice and it is still being heard. Hebrews knows that crying blood and sets a better word against it, for the new covenant brings *the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel* (Hebrews 12:24). And Abel does not cry alone. Under the altar the slain make the same suit: *the souls of them that were slain for the word of Elohim (God)... cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Yahuah (Lord), holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?* (Revelation 6:9-10). The blood of the righteous is kept in remembrance, and it pleads from the holding-place until the great day answers it.
note: Old 22:12 quote was corrupt wording of 22:5; re-formed on the live 22:5, 22:7, 22:12.

title: The bright spring for the righteous, the sinners set apart
summary_md: The hollows are not one undivided pit. They are sorted by the way each one walked: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9), and another hollow is kept for those who died with their account unsettled: *And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.* (1 Enoch 22:10), *Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.* (1 Enoch 22:11). Abraham draws the same line for the rich man: *Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented* (Luke 16:25). The righteous are comforted at the spring and the sinner is in pain, and what divides them is the way each one kept. And the earth itself has swallowed the rebel living before — when Korah's company *go down quick into the pit* (Numbers 16:30), they *went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation* (Numbers 16:33). The division is not arbitrary. It follows the covenant. The righteous who kept the way are held at the bright spring, the transgressors are set apart in pain, and all of them alike are waiting for the great day of judgement.
note: Quotes on the live 22:9-11 (old 22:16-18 gone), put in verse order; prose smoothed.

title: The fire that runs without resting — the fire in the west that drives the luminaries
summary_md: At the western ends of the earth Enoch sees a fire that never stops: *And I saw a burning fire which ran without resting, and paused not from its course day or night but (ran) regularly.* (1 Enoch 23:2). He asks what it is, and Raguel tells him: *Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said unto me: ‘This course of fire which thou hast seen is the fire in the west which persecutes all the luminaries of heaven.’* (1 Enoch 23:4). The fire that drives the lights of heaven on their courses is no strange revelation. The canon's sun is driven the same way. Psalm 19 sees the same untiring runner: *In them hath he set a tabernacle for the sun,* (Psalms 19:4), *Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to run a race.* (Psalms 19:5), *His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it: and there is nothing hid from the heat thereof.* (Psalms 19:6), the very circuit to the ends of the earth that Enoch is shown. Psalm 104 says the flame is a servant of Yahuah (God), who *maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:* (Psalms 104:4) and who *appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalms 104:19). The fire does not burn loose. It runs an appointed course and it presses the luminaries to run theirs, and the sun has never once left that course. The Watchers did.
note: Old 23:4 ("the fire which surrounds the sun") was corrupt; live 23:4 is the fire in the west which persecutes all the luminaries. Re-formed and retitled to the live words.

title: The six portals and the chariots of the sun, moon, and stars
summary_md: The fire Enoch sees at the western ends of the earth is the fire that keeps the lights of heaven moving: *Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said unto me: ‘This course of fire which thou hast seen is the fire in the west which persecutes all the luminaries of heaven.’* (1 Enoch 23:4). The book of the luminaries later shows the machinery those lights are driven through. They have gates: *And I saw six portals in which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets: and the moon rises and sets in these portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west, and all following each other in accurately corresponding order: also many windows to the right and left of these portals.* (1 Enoch 72:3). They have chariots: *The chariot on which he ascends, the wind drives, and the sun goes down from the heaven and returns through the north in order to reach the east, and is so guided that he comes to the appropriate (lit. ‘that’) portal and shines in the face of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:5), *And I saw chariots in the heaven, running in the world, above those portals in which revolve the stars that never set.* (1 Enoch 75:8). And every one of them has a keeper: *For the signs and the times and the years and the days the angel Uriel showed to me, whom Yahuah (Lord) of glory hath set for ever over all the luminaries of the heaven, in the heaven and in the world, that they should rule on the face of the heaven and be seen on the earth, and be leaders for the day and the night, i.e. the sun, moon, and stars, and all the ministering creatures which make their revolution in all the chariots of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 75:3). The portals and the chariots are the appointed gates and the appointed carriages through which the lights keep the laws Uriel showed Enoch, and the fire in the west is what will not let them rest.
note: Old 23:5-6 are gone and 72:4 was misquoted; re-formed from the live 23:4 into 72:3, 72:5, 75:8, 75:3. Duplicate 72:3 quote removed.

title: All the stars rise and set in their order — the decree that shall not pass
summary_md: The fire that drives the luminaries drives them into order, and Enoch had opened his whole book on that order: *Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.* (1 Enoch 2:1). The book of the luminaries measures how exact that obedience is: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). This is the ordinance of the fourth day: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). Psalm 148 commands these same obedient lights to praise, *Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light.* (Psalms 148:3), and gives the reason they can be commanded at all: *He hath also stablished them for ever and ever: he hath made a decree which shall not pass.* (Psalms 148:6). Then Yahuah (God) ties that unbreakable order to the continuance of his people. He *giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night* (Jeremiah 31:35), and swears, *If those ordinances depart from before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), then the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.* (Jeremiah 31:36). Enoch turns the same comparison on his hearers: *And all His works go on thus from year to year for ever, and all the tasks which they accomplish for Him, and their tasks change not, but according as Elohim (God) hath ordained so is it done.* (1 Enoch 5:2), *But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), But ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words With your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.* (1 Enoch 5:4). The stars keeping their course is the standing pledge that the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) is never cast off, and the same stars are the standing rebuke to a people who will not keep theirs.
note: Old 23:8 and 75:15 were invented (chapter 23 has four verses); re-formed on the live 2:1, 74:12, 5:2, 5:4 (live text), keeping the canon witnesses.

title: Reserved till the great judgement: the tree given to the righteous and elect
summary_md: The tree is sealed until the reckoning: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). The same gate stands at the end of Scripture: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14). The right to the tree belongs to those who *do his commandments*, so the Torah is still standing at the gate of the city, and the ones who keep it are the ones who were chosen, which is why they keep it. Isaiah measures the elect's portion by that same tree: *they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands* (Isaiah 65:22), the same fruit Enoch says is *for food to the elect*. And 2 Esdras describes its healing virtue laid up for the righteous: *they shall have the tree of life for an ointment of sweet savour; they shall neither labour, nor be weary* (2 Esdras 2:12), the very fragrance Enoch says will be in their bones. The tree is not for whoever reaches for it. It is given, after the judgement has separated, to a people who were chosen, the righteous and the elect, and it is carried into the holy place of Yahuah (God) where they will eat from it.
note: Quote already on the live 25:4-5 (old 24:10 gone); prose smoothed.

title: Long life and no sorrow: the days of the fathers restored
summary_md: Enoch closes with the blessing the tree secures for the elect: *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). The prophets sang the same end of sorrow: *He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it* (Isaiah 25:8). John saw it fulfilled in the restored creation: *And Elohim (God) shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4), which is Enoch's *no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity* said again. And the curse that shortened the patriarchs' years is lifted at the throne where the tree stands: *And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him* (Revelation 22:3). The long life *such as thy fathers lived* is the span of the first fathers given back, and it is the same end the whole canon is waiting for.
note: Quote already on the live 25:6 (old 24:12 gone); prose smoothed.

title: Prepared, created, and promised — Enoch blesses the Eternal King for what is laid up for the righteous
summary_md: When Michael has finished telling Enoch what the tree is for, Enoch does the only thing left to do: *Then blessed I the Elohim (God) of Glory, the Eternal King, who hath prepared such things for the righteous, and hath created them and promised to give to them.* (1 Enoch 25:7). Three things are said in one breath, that the tree and the holy place were prepared, that they were created, and that they were promised. What was promised is what Michael had just described: *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5), *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6). Isaiah blesses the same preparation in almost the same words: *For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the eye seen, O Elohim (God), beside you, what he has prepared for him that waits for him.* (Isaiah 64:4), and Paul carries Isaiah's line to the assembly: *But as it is written, Eye has not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which Elohim (God) has prepared for them that love him.* (1 Corinthians 2:9). Yahusha (Jesus) says the preparing is his own work: *In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.* (John 14:2). And the tree itself is the one driven out of reach in the garden, *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* (Genesis 3:24), and held out again at the end to the one who holds on: *To him that overcomes will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). Enoch saw it already prepared, already created, and already promised, and he blessed the King who keeps his word.
note: The old summary was written on the corrupt chapter 25 (a duplicate of chapter 15) and carried a "Note for Yoshi". The evil-spirits thought lives at 15:8-11 and is carried by the chapter-15/16 threads. Re-formed on the live 25:5-7 with Isaiah 64:4, 1 Corinthians 2:9, John 14:2, Genesis 3:24, Revelation 2:7 from the index; new title.

title: The middle of the earth and the holy mountain — Zion at the navel
summary_md: Enoch is carried to the centre of the world: *And I went from thence to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place in which there were trees with branches abiding and blooming [of a dismembered tree].* (1 Enoch 26:1), *And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:2). The Tanakh sets Jerusalem in exactly that place, at the midst of the nations: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her.* (Ezekiel 5:5), and it names the regathered people as those *that dwell in the midst of the land.* (Ezekiel 38:12). The holy mountain is Zion, of whom the psalmist sings *Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.* (Psalm 48:2), the place where *Elohim (God) is my King of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.* (Psalm 74:12). Jubilees says it most plainly of all: *And he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of Yahuah (God), and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion–the centre of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other.* (Jubilees 8:18). The blessed place at the middle of the earth with the holy mountain in it is Zion, and Enoch saw it before there was a city on it.
note: Old 26:1-2 quote was corrupt wording; re-quoted the live 26:1 and 26:2 in full; close smoothed.

title: The stream under the holy mountain, and the dry ravines where no tree is planted
summary_md: Under the holy mountain a stream runs out to the east, and the land around it is cut by ravines: *And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:2), *And I saw towards the east another mountain higher than this, and between them a deep and narrow ravine: in it also ran a stream underneath the mountain.* (1 Enoch 26:3), *And to the west thereof there was another mountain, lower than the former and of small elevation, and a ravine deep and dry between them: and another deep and dry ravine was at the extremities of the three mountains.* (1 Enoch 26:4). Ezekiel is shown that same water coming out from under the holy mountain on the east side: *Afterward he brought me again unto the door of the house; and, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward: for the forefront of the house stood toward the east, and the waters came down from under from the right side of the house, at the south side of the altar.* (Ezekiel 47:1), and he sees what grows wherever it runs: *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* (Ezekiel 47:12). John sees the source of it: *And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of Elohim (God) and of the Lamb.* (Revelation 22:1). Where that water runs, the trees abide and bloom, as Enoch saw at the blessed place. Where it does not, the ravines are deep and dry and *trees were not planted upon them* (1 Enoch 26:5). The man of the covenant is himself such a tree: *And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither* (Psalm 1:3). The righteous flourish where the living water of the sanctuary runs out from Zion, and nothing grows in the dry ravines beside it.
note: Old 26:3-4 quote ("fragrant trees by the streams") was invented; the live 26:2-5 is the stream, the mountains and the dry ravines. Re-formed on the live text with Ezekiel 47:1 and Revelation 22:1 from the index; new title.

title: The throne-mountain and the tree of life reserved for the great judgement
summary_md: Michael unveils what the mountain and the tree truly are: *And he answered saying: ‘This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Elohim (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (Lord) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.* (1 Enoch 25:3), and of the fragrant tree: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy. Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:4-5). This is the tree of life of Eden, *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9) — guarded from mortal hands after the fall *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and restored at the end to the holy city: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month* (Revelation 22:2), given to those who keep covenant — *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.* (Revelation 22:14). The long life Enoch promises the elect, *Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, And into the holy place shall they enter; And its fragrance shall be in their bones, And they shall live a long life on earth, Such as thy fathers lived: And in their days shall no sorrow or plague Or torment or calamity touch them.’* (1 Enoch 25:6), is Isaiah's restored Yashar'el (Israel), *for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands* (Isaiah 65:22), and John's new world where *there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain* (Revelation 21:4). The tree is withheld until the great judgement and then given to the elect, and every book that touches it says the same.
note: Old 26:7-10 citations were corrupt; quotes now on the live 25:3, 25:4-5, 25:6; prose smoothed.

title: The accursed valley beside the blessed land — where the hard-mouthed are gathered for judgement
summary_md: Enoch has just seen the blessed land at the middle of the earth, and beside it something that does not fit: *Then said I: ‘For what object is this blessed land, which is entirely filled with trees, and this accursed valley between?’* (1 Enoch 27:1). Uriel tells him what the valley is for: *Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: ‘This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against Yahuah (Lord) unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.* (1 Enoch 27:2). The valley under the holy mountain is where the prophets put the judgement too. Joel hears Yahuah (God) say, *I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Yashar'el (Israel), whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.* (Joel 3:2), and again, *Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about.* (Joel 3:12). Zechariah sees the ground itself opened for it: *And his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east, and the mount of Olives shall cleave in the midst thereof toward the east and toward the west, and there shall be a very great valley; and half of the mountain shall remove toward the north, and half of it toward the south.* (Zechariah 14:4). The ones gathered there are named by what came out of their mouths, hard words against his glory, and Enoch had already said who those are: *But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), But ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words With your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.* (1 Enoch 5:4). The blessed land and the accursed valley sit side by side on purpose. The throne-mountain is where the Eternal King comes down, and the valley at its foot is where the ones who cursed him are gathered to meet him.
note: Old summary was written on the corrupt chapter 27 (throne-mountain, which lives at 25:3 and is carried by the chapter-25/26 threads); the live chapter 27 is the accursed valley. Re-formed on 27:1-2 with 1 Enoch 5:4 (live text) and Joel 3:2, 3:12, Zechariah 14:4 from the index; degraded close removed; new title.

title: The spectacle of judgement in the valley — the merciful bless the Eternal King for the lot he assigned
summary_md: Uriel does not stop at the gathering. He tells Enoch what the valley becomes on the day: *In the last days there shall be upon them the spectacle of righteous judgement in the presence of the righteous for ever: here shall the merciful bless Yahuah (Lord) of glory, the Eternal King. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be the place of their habitation.* (1 Enoch 27:3), *In the days of judgement over the former, they shall bless Him for the mercy in accordance with which He has assigned them (their lot).’* (1 Enoch 27:4). Two companies stand in the same place and see the same thing, the accursed under judgement and the merciful blessing him for it. Isaiah ends his whole book on that scene: *And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.* (Isaiah 66:24). Yahusha (Jesus) takes Isaiah's words for the same valley: *And if your hand offend you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:* (Mark 9:43), *Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched.* (Mark 9:44). The hell he names there is this valley at the foot of Jerusalem, and the ones who look on are the righteous Isaiah and Enoch both saw. What Enoch does when he hears it is what the merciful will do when they see it: *Then I blessed Yahuah (Lord) of Glory and set forth His glory and lauded Him gloriously.* (1 Enoch 27:5). Judgement in the valley and blessing on the mountain are one day, and the ones who kept his word bless him for the lot he assigned.
note: Old summary was written on the corrupt chapter 27 (the fragrant tree, which lives at 24:4 and 25:4-5 and is carried by the chapter-24/25 threads); re-formed on the live 27:3-5 with Isaiah 66:24 and Mark 9:43-44 from the index; new title.
